doc.title: Eddie Locke interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York, NY, January 13, 2001

chapter: Detroit and the Bop and Locke act
title: Leonard Sillman audition and the act's tunes
summary: The act auditions for Leonard Sillman's New Faces, and Locke describes their original tunes and synchronized two-kit drumming.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Well Tommy Flanagan, you know he used to accompany us and help us too. And one time, you remember Leonard Sillman?

Smart Affairs? He used to sing. That’s where Eartha Kitt came from, Robert Clary. He was called Leonard Sillman. He would get all these young people, he would find these “New Faces.” He called them like “New Faces” of 1949, then 1950, and every year he would audition and then he would put a show together and take them around the country. Eartha Kitt — all these people came from that guy, that “New Faces.” Robert Clary, a couple of those guys. But anyway, we auditioned for him. And Tommy was our accompanist. And it was in a theater so Tommy was like down in the pit and we were up on the stage and he was sitting right there. So Tommy says “yeah, man, you guys came out and you were singing and he was smiling and everything. You played the drums, he was smiling,” he said “then you started telling those sad jokes, man” and he said — Tommy always tells everybody that. He said they saw him scratch your name off.
What were a couple of the tunes that you would have done in that act?

Our opening tune was called “Drummer Man.” We wrote that. And then we did things like “Lover” for the drum pieces. We were synchronized drumming. Where we did — we had two complete drum sets and each hand was doing the same thing. You know what I mean?
Yeah. So it was not like today, people have got video. I sure wish I had a video or something of it.
It would be. I’ve got some still pictures, a couple of still pictures, but that’s all.
